items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A slow tortoise raced a boastful hare. The hare ran ahead, then napped, sure he would win. The tortoise kept plodding and crossed the finish line first.

What is the lesson of this fable?
A) Naps are good
B) Slow and steady wins the race
C) Hares are fast
D) Races are fun
items.answer: B) Slow and steady wins the race

steps: The tortoise "kept plodding" while the hare napped.
Steady effort beat speed plus laziness.
So the lesson is B.
solution.answer: B) Slow and steady wins the race

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Mia wanted the new bike now, but Dad said to save her allowance. Week by week her jar filled, and after two months she bought it herself and felt proud.

What is the central message?
A) Bikes are expensive
B) Saving and patience pay off
C) Dads are strict
D) Two months is long
items.answer: B) Saving and patience pay off

steps: Mia saved "week by week" and finally bought the bike herself.
Her patience and saving led to the reward.
The message is B.
solution.answer: B) Saving and patience pay off

items.prompt:
Read the folktale.

A proud rooster laughed at the plain brown hen. But when a fox came, the quiet hen's warning cluck saved the whole farmyard.

What lesson does this teach?
A) Roosters are loud
B) Do not judge someone by how they look
C) Foxes are sneaky
D) Farms have many animals
items.answer: B) Do not judge someone by how they look

steps: The proud rooster mocked the plain hen.
Yet the plain hen "saved the whole farmyard."
So do not judge by looks; the answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Do not judge someone by how they look

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Carlos always did his homework the minute he got home, while his friends waited until midnight and complained they were tired. On test day, Carlos was rested and ready.

Which lesson does the story best teach?
A) Homework is boring
B) Doing work early makes life easier
C) Tests are hard
D) Friends stay up late
items.answer: B) Doing work early makes life easier

steps: Carlos did homework "the minute he got home" and was "rested and ready."
His friends waited and were tired.
The lesson is that doing work early helps, so B.
solution.answer: B) Doing work early makes life easier

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

The wind and the sun argued over who was stronger. The wind blew hard to tear off a traveler's coat, but the man only clutched it tighter. Then the sun shone warmly, and the man took the coat off himself.

What does this fable teach?
A) Wind is powerful
B) Gentleness works better than force
C) Coats keep you warm
D) The sun is hot
items.answer: B) Gentleness works better than force

steps: The forceful wind failed to remove the coat.
The gentle, warm sun succeeded.
So gentleness beat force; the answer is B.
solution.answer: B) Gentleness works better than force

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Tani found a wallet full of cash on the sidewalk. She could have kept it, but she turned it in at the front desk. The owner was so grateful he told everyone how honest she was.

What is the central message of this story?
A) Wallets hold money
B) Honesty is worth more than what you could take
C) Sidewalks are busy
D) Owners forget things
items.answer: B) Honesty is worth more than what you could take

steps: Tani "could have kept it" but chose to turn it in.
Her honesty earned respect and thanks.
The message is that honesty matters most, so B.
solution.answer: B) Honesty is worth more than what you could take

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every morning Grandpa fed the crows, and the family called it a waste of bread. But one winter he slipped on the ice, and it was the crows' loud calling that brought neighbors running to help him.

Which sentence best states the story's message?
A) Crows are noisy birds
B) Feeding animals wastes food
C) Small kindnesses can come back to help you
D) Winter ice is dangerous
items.answer: C) Small kindnesses can come back to help you

steps: Grandpa's daily kindness to the crows seemed like "a waste."
Later the crows' calling "brought neighbors running to help him."
His kindness returned to help him, so C.
solution.answer: C) Small kindnesses can come back to help you

items.prompt:
Read the myth.

Proud King Midas wished everything he touched would turn to gold. His wish came true, but soon his food, his cup, even his daughter turned hard and gold. He begged to have the gift taken away.

What lesson does this myth teach?
A) Gold is valuable
B) Kings are powerful
C) Being greedy can cost you what matters most
D) Wishes always come true
items.answer: C) Being greedy can cost you what matters most

steps: Midas greedily wished for endless gold.
The gift ruined his food and even his daughter.
Greed cost him what mattered, so C.
solution.answer: C) Being greedy can cost you what matters most
